drafted_from: tool:github:docling-project-docling's row in tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json (job, run, get_it, needs) and its sources row in sources.json; the command is the row's own run line with synthetic names filled in. What it prints or writes is read from the tool's documented behavior; the folder test test/index-github-tools.test.mjs only checks the row, never runs docling.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use docling on my computer to read a document (PDF: the file is price-list.pdf." It reads the row, installs docling if it is missing, runs it on that one file and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: docling is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on the one file or address it is handed.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use docling on price-list.pdf". It reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:docling-project-docling"}.
2. It checks that python are on your computer, and if docling is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/docling-project/docling.git ; pip install docling.
3. It runs the row's command with your file in place of {input}: docling price-list.pdf
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. Trillion runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: docling on a two page PDF price list with one table
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json: tool:github:docling-project-docling runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got docling in, the command line: docling price-list.pdf  (synthetic input: a two page PDF price list with one table).
worked_examples.hands_back: docling reads price-list.pdf and writes price-list.md in the folder it ran in: the text as Markdown with the table rebuilt as a Markdown table (one "|" row per price line).
